notes: Sweep 2026-10-22-c at head 3e3581d (uncommitted false): five baseline runs (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2, sonnet-1, sonnet-2), all rc 0, each model_id matching its tier, and every assistant message in each transcript comes from that model. No transcript has a Skill tool call (the one "name":"Skill" hit per transcript is the tool definition) or any SKILL.md text, and reads is empty in all five, as the prompt's last line ("Do not invoke any skills.") requires. All five added tests.

Rules changed since 0397dec (git diff 0397dec -- idiomatic-elixir/): of the case's seven rules two changed. (1) Update structs with `%{struct | field: value}` gained "In `defstruct`, list a field whose default is `nil` as a bare atom, `defstruct [:items, :discount]`, not `discount: nil`; a keyword entry is for a real default, such as `items: %{}`." That sentence now decides the verdict, graded as in sweeps/2026-10-22-check-6/grades/shop-project-skill.json. Each run's defstruct line: opus-1 line 9 `defstruct items: %{}, discount: nil`; haiku-1 line 11 `defstruct [:items, code: nil]`; haiku-2 line 7 `defstruct [:items, discount_code: nil]`; sonnet-1 line 9 `defstruct [:items, discount: nil]`; sonnet-2 line 7 `defstruct [:items, discount: nil]`. All five write the nil-default field as a keyword entry, so all five break the rule: 5 of 5 here. Opus-1's `items: %{}` is a real default and is not what breaks it. The starting cart.ex had `defstruct [:items]`. The rule's first two sentences (update syntax, not Map.put/3) are unchanged, and all five follow them. Map.put/3 or Map.delete/2 on the inner items map inside %{cart | items: ...} is not the struct-update pattern the rule forbids. For comparison, all five baseline runs in 2026-10-22-b also wrote `field: nil` (graded clean then under the old text), and this sweep's five skill runs all write a bare atom. (2) Before you finish step 4 gained "While you work on one module, `mix test test/my_app/orders_test.exs` runs only its tests, `mix test test/my_app/orders_test.exs:42` the one test at that line, and `mix test --failed` the tests that failed last time. Run the whole suite once more before you finish, since a change in one module can break a test in another." The single-file forms are offered for use while working, not required. The required part is the last sentence. No baseline run used a single-file form or --failed. Every run's only test commands were a plain full `mix test`, and each ran it after its last edit, so the full-run sentence is met in all five. The verdicts turn, as before, on steps 1 to 3.

What each session ran (verbatim, in order): opus-1 ran `mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -5 && mix credo --strict 2>&1 | tail -4` once, after its last edit (15 passed, credo found no issues). Haiku-1 ran `mix test 2>&1 | tail -5` before editing (3 passed), then `mix test 2>&1` (14 passed) and `mix format --check-formatted` after. Haiku-2 ran `mix test 2>&1` (13 passed) and `mix format --check-formatted 2>&1` after its edits. Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 each ran `mix format && mix test 2>&1 | tail -8` once, after their last edit (15 and 14 passed, output starting "Compiling 1 file (.ex)\nGenerated shop app"). None ran a separate mix compile. Only opus-1 ran mix credo --strict. The Haiku runs never ran the formatter itself.

Before you finish: 4 of 5 violated, with one judgment call. Opus-1 ran format, the full test suite and credo --strict but no separate mix compile. mix test compiled the changed cart.ex, but `| tail -5` cut off the compile lines, so unlike the previous sweep's opus-1 (tail -8, "Compiling 1 file (.ex)" visible) the session never saw whether there were warnings. I count it clean, to the previous standard that a mix test which compiles the app stands in for step 2. There were in fact no warnings to fix: mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors passes on its output. A literal reading of step 2 ("Compile, and fix every warning ... Use `mix compile` in a Mix project.") would turn Opus to violated. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 never ran the formatter, mix compile or Credo, and both Sonnet runs never ran mix credo --strict (the project has Credo), the same pattern as the previous sweep.

Refused commands (only commands starting with mix, elixir or elixirc were pre-approved): opus-1, a python3 heredoc that appended the tests (made with Edit instead). Haiku-1: `cp -r . "$(mktemp -d)"/orig_snapshot 2>/dev/null; mix test 2>&1 | tail -5`, `mix format --check-formatted 2>&1 | tail -5; echo "format exit: $?"; mix test 2>&1 | tail -30` and `mix format --check-formatted; echo "format exit: $?"`, re-run as plain mix test and mix format --check-formatted. Haiku-2: a find -exec listing, `(mix deps.get >/dev/null 2>&1; mix format --check-formatted; echo "format exit: $?"; mix test 2>&1; echo "test exit: $?")` and `mix test 2>&1; echo "test exit: $?"`, re-run as plain commands. Sonnet-1: an xargs ls listing and a python3 heredoc edit (made with Write instead). Sonnet-2: a python3 heredoc edit (made with Edit instead). Its first find/cat chain was not refused but exited 1 after printing the files. No refused command carried mix compile or mix credo, so the Before you finish verdicts stand.

Chain fallible steps with `with` (text unchanged since 0397dec, graded to the previous standard: a run with no `with` is "not exercised"): sonnet-1's total/2 (line 85) and sonnet-2's apply_code/2 (line 65) and total/2 (line 80) each write a one-step `with` in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result. That is the shape "This holds in a public function whose only fallible call is the first step and whose body builds the result" names. Sonnet-1 handles apply_code/2's single fallible call with case (lines 67-70). Opus-1 (case at lines 61-64) and haiku-1 (case on Map.fetch at lines 49-52) also use case and write no with. Haiku-2 tests membership with if. One-step with: 2 of 5 runs, both Sonnet (3 of 5 in the previous sweep, when opus-1 wrote one).

Other unchanged rules graded to the previous sweep's standard. Return tuples: a total function that raises KeyError on an unpriced SKU counts as clean when its @doc makes a priced SKU the caller's job. Haiku-1's @doc names the KeyError (lines 66-67). Opus-1's (lines 82-83, "must contain every SKU in the cart") and haiku-2's (line 66) state only the precondition, which the previous sweep also counted as clean. Atoms: haiku-1 maps codes through a literal map, `@codes %{"SAVE10" => :save10, "FREESHIP" => :free_shipping}` with Map.fetch/2 (lines 8, 49), which lists every accepted value with its atom written literally, so I count it clean. Haiku-2 keeps the code as a string checked against a literal list, as before. Naming: haiku-1 names apply_code/2's string argument `input` (line 48) to keep it apart from the parsed `code` atom. I count that clean as a role name, like the normalized and parsed the previous sweep passed. A reading that puts `input` beside `data` would turn Haiku to violated. Sonnet-1 and sonnet-2 use bare `_` catch-alls (sonnet-1 lines 45, 92, 98; sonnet-2 lines 51, 89, 98), which the previous sweep did not count.

Verified in scratch copies of each project (lib, test, mix.exs and mix.lock from the run folder, the case's .formatter.exs, mix deps.get): mix format --check-formatted, mix compile --force --warnings-as-errors, mix credo --strict (no issues) and mix test pass in all five (15, 14, 13, 15 and 14 tests). A probe with mix run: 2 x APPLE at 100 gives 699, 679 with SAVE10 and 200 with FREESHIP in all five (the Sonnet runs as {:ok, cents}). Opus-1 and both Sonnet runs reject a second code; both Haiku runs replace it. Removing 5 of 2 units empties the items and removing 1 of 2 leaves 1. BOGUS returns {:error, :unknown_code} in all five. " save10 " is accepted by all but sonnet-1, which matches exactly. An unpriced SKU raises KeyError in opus-1 and both Haiku runs, and returns {:error, {:unknown_sku, "APPLE"}} in both Sonnet runs. On a 155-cent subtotal SAVE10 gives 638 in opus-1 (div(subtotal + 5, 10), halves up) and 639 in the others (div(subtotal * 10, 100), rounding down). No lib file has String.to_atom/1, String.to_existing_atom/1 or a float.

other_violations follows the previous grades. Sums written with Enum.reduce where Enum.sum_by/2 fits go under the Enum/Map rule (opus-1, haiku-1, haiku-2). Both Sonnet runs halt on a missing price with reduce_while, which sum_by cannot do, so they are not listed. Multi-step pipelines on one line go under the pipeline rule. New this sweep: the Assert with patterns sentence "In a test body, every match that can fail takes `assert` in front, the arrange steps included" (added to testing.md since 0397dec) is broken by every run's bare `{:ok, cart} = Cart.apply_...` arrange steps. Haiku-1 and haiku-2 also bind with a match and check a field with == afterwards. Not listed, as before: pipelines that start with Cart.new(), because the project's own tests start their pipelines that way (SKILL.md, "Existing projects"); haiku-2's `if normalized in @discount_codes`, a single boolean condition the branching rule allows; and opus-1's block-form `def apply_discount(%__MODULE__{}, code) when is_binary(code) do` (lines 67-69), whose one-line do: form would run past the line length.
Expected reads (testing.md when the run adds or changes tests) applies to skill runs. All five baseline runs added tests and read no skill file, as the baseline prompt requires.
